events.label: founding
events.text: Squadron established as Patrol Squadron 25 at NAAS Harvey Point, North Carolina.

evidence.quote: established as Patrol Squadron 25 ( VP-25 ) on 20 April 1944
20 April 1944 : VP-25 was established at NAAS Harvey Point , North Carolina

events.text: Squadron placed under operational control of FAW-5.

evidence.quote: 20 April 1944 : VP-25 was established at NAAS Harvey Point , North Carolina , under the operational control of FAW-5

events.label: aircraft_type
events.text: Squadron assigned PBM-3D as its aircraft type.

evidence.quote: PBM-3D - 20 April 1944

events.text: Squadron sent to NAS Key West, Florida, for ASW training.

evidence.quote: 26 June 1944 : The squadron was sent to NAS Key West , Florida

events.text: Squadron returned to NAAS Harvey Point after training.

evidence.quote: returning to NAAS Harvey Point on 4 July 1944

events.text: Squadron departed Harvey Point for NAS Alameda, California.

evidence.quote: The squadron remained at NAAS Harvey Point until 18 August 1944 , when it departed for NAS Alameda , California

events.text: Squadron reported to FAW-14 at NAS Alameda for orders.

evidence.quote: 21 August – 29 September 1944 : VP-25 reported to FAW-14 , NAS Alameda for orders
NAS Alameda , California - 21 August 1944

events.text: Squadron departed for Hawaii and arrived at NAS Kaneohe Bay.

evidence.quote: Orders were issued for departure on 15 September 1944
NAS Kaneohe Bay , Hawaii - 15 September 1944

events.text: Squadron redesignated Patrol Bombing Squadron 25 (VPB-25).

evidence.quote: redesignated Patrol Bombing Squadron 25 ( VPB-25 ) on 1 October 1944
1 October – 14 November 1944 : VP-25 was redesignated VPB-25

events.text: Squadron placed under operational control of FAW-2.

evidence.quote: 1 October – 14 November 1944 : VP-25 was redesignated VPB-25 , coming under the operational control of FAW-2

events.text: Squadron received orders to report to the combat zone.

evidence.quote: until orders were received for the squadron to report to the combat zone on 14 November 1944

events.text: Squadron departed Hawaii for San Pedro Bay, Leyte, Philippines.

evidence.quote: 15 November – 1 December 1944 : VPB-25 departed Hawaii for San Pedro Bay , Leyte , Philippines

events.label: combat_operations
events.text: Squadron began its first daytime combat sector patrols.

evidence.quote: VPB-25 began its first daytime combat sector patrols on 1 December 1944

events.text: Squadron ordered to transfer operations to Mangarin Bay, Mindoro.

evidence.quote: 25–29 December 1944 : VPB-25 received orders to transfer its operations to Mangarin Bay , Mindoro , Philippines

events.text: Squadron aircrews flew from San Pedro Bay to rejoin at Mangarin Bay.

evidence.quote: On 29 December 1944 , the squadron aircrews flew from San Pedro Bay to rejoin the rest of the squadron

events.label: operations
events.text: Squadron began sector searches from Mangarin Bay.

evidence.quote: The squadron began conducting sector searches from the new location the next day

events.text: Squadron transferred to Jinamoc Seaplane Base, Leyte.

evidence.quote: 6–25 February 1945 : VPB-25 was transferred to Jinamoc Seaplane Base , Leyte , Philippines

events.text: Squadron placed under operational control of FAW-10 for courier flights.

evidence.quote: 6–25 February 1945 : VPB-25 was transferred to Jinamoc Seaplane Base , Leyte , Philippines , under the operational control of FAW-10

events.label: aircraft_type
events.text: Squadron assigned new Martin PBM-3D2 Mariner aircraft.

evidence.quote: PBM-3D2 - 6 February 1945
After receiving and checking out its new Martin PBM-3D2 Mariners

events.text: Mangarin Bay detachment ordered to relocate to Manila Bay.

evidence.quote: 7 March 1945 : The squadron’s Mangarin Bay detachment received orders to relocate to Manila Bay

events.text: Cavite detachment relocated to Lingayen Gulf, relieving VPB-17.

evidence.quote: 24–28 June 1945 : The Cavite detachment was relocated to Lingayen Gulf

events.label: operations
events.text: Black Cat nighttime antishipping operations commenced.

evidence.quote: Operations commenced with the squadron conducting Black Cat , nighttime , operations against enemy shipping on 28 June 1945

events.text: Cavite detachment transferred to Puerto Princesa, Palawan.

evidence.quote: 9 July 1945 : The Cavite detachment was transferred to Puerto Princesa , Palawan , Philippines

events.text: Cavite detachment relieved and rejoined squadron at Lingayen Gulf.

evidence.quote: This detachment was relieved on 23 July to rejoin the rest of the squadron at Lingayen Gulf

events.text: Half of squadron shifted to USS San Pablo at Lingayen Gulf.

evidence.quote: 20 August – 3 September 1945 : USS San Pablo arrived on station at Lingayen Gulf to relieve USS Currituck

events.text: Tawi-Tawi detachment shifted to the relieving tender.

evidence.quote: USS Pocomoke was relieved by on 3 September 1945 , and the Tawi-Tawi detachment shifted aboard the latter

events.text: Squadron assigned duty with occupation forces in Japan.

evidence.quote: 22 March 1946 : VPB-25 was assigned duty with the occupation forces in Japan through 1 May 1946

events.text: Home port assigned as NAS Kaneohe Bay, Hawaii.

evidence.quote: NAS Kaneohe Bay - May 1946

events.text: Home port assigned as NAS Alameda, California.

evidence.quote: NAS Alameda - May 1946

events.text: Squadron occupation duty in Japan ended.

evidence.quote: assigned duty with the occupation forces in Japan through 1 May 1946

events.text: Squadron redesignated Patrol Squadron 25 (VP-25).

evidence.quote: redesignated Patrol Squadron 25 ( VP-25 ) on 15 May 1946

events.label: disestablishment
events.text: Squadron disestablished.

evidence.quote: disestablished on 28 June 1946
28 June 1946 : VP-25 was disestablished

undated_mentions: Further operational training near Hilo Bay, Hawaii
Dumbo air-sea rescue missions from Lingayen Gulf
Tawi-Tawi detachment antishipping and surveillance patrols
